solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sanctimonious person repeatedly turning prison sitcom on and off?

indicators.note: switching back and forth again and again suggests taking letters in a regular pattern
one letter kept, the next dropped, so the odd-numbered letters are taken

parts.note: Porridge was the BBC prison comedy starring Ronnie Barker

explanation.surface: Someone holier-than-thou keeps flicking a prison comedy on and off the television.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is a 1970s British TV sitcom set in a prison; 'repeatedly turning ... on and off' keeps its 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-righteous, priggish person is smugly moralistic, which is what sanctimonious describes.

clue.text: Women having a challenge to circumvent computer plug-ins?

indicators.note: to go round something, so the first pieces surround the abbreviation

parts.note: a dare is a challenge to do something risky

explanation.surface: Women dare each other to get round some computer add-ons.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising software is often bundled into browser extensions and add-on programs, hence the question mark on the loose description.

clue.text: Originator of the law exploiting beer and petrol

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are worked over and put to new use as a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone credited with founding a legal principle that takes advantage of beer and petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The law' is slang for the police: Sir Robert Peel founded London's Metropolitan Police in 1829, hence 'bobbies'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian Home Secretary created the modern police force, the 'law' in informal speech, so he originated it.

clue.text: Once again it's nice engaging servant when growing up

indicators.note: holding within, so the exclamation wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an exclamation of pleasure, 'Ah!', says that something is nice

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a serf was a feudal servant bound to the land

explanation.surface: Once more it's lovely to take on a domestic as they grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anew or from scratch means doing it over again.

clue.text: Wire-tapper will roll radio up

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: this word is the first half of the 9-across answer, so it stands for the clue number nine

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper will roll up a radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference trick: 'radio' is the answer at 9 across, so it means NINE, and 'up' turns that into ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping a phone line is done to eavesdrop secretly, so that is what such a snooper will do.

clue.text: Whip round for a little fresh salmon?

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are read backwards
only a small part of the words is taken, a run hidden across them

explanation.surface: A collection for some fresh salmon, perhaps for a fishmonger's leaving present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' looks like the definition (a collection); only 'Whip' is, and 'round' reverses the run HSAL found in 'fresH SALmon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip or lash is a flexible cord used for flogging; both also mean strike with one.

clue.text: I ask for a lift as crone cuts Americans' gullets

indicators.note: breaks into, so the old woman sits within the other letters
lifted up in a down clue, so the words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker asks for a ride as an old woman slashes American throats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a lift' reads the first two pieces upwards in this down clue. The spelling with a single E, not OE, is the American one, hence 'Americans''.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet is the food pipe, the oesophagus; US spelling drops the O and this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Eighties tennis ace calms military arrangements

parts.note: Ivan Lendl was world number one in men's tennis during the 1980s
eases means soothes or calms

explanation.surface: A top 1980s tennis player soothes nerves before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lend-Lease programme supplied Allied forces with war materiel in World War II, so these are military supply deals.

clue.text: Mayday?

parts.note: the international distress call is an emergency signal sent by wireless; read another way, it is a clock that wakes you on a May morning

explanation.walkthrough: Two sides to one word: 'Mayday' is a distress call sent over the airwaves, and a wake-up clock-wireless rousing you on a day in May.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mayday is literally an alarm raised by wireless, and the joke also suggests a clock radio going off.

clue.text: End of week box does not contain dry chicken feed!

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated, ends the working week

indicators.note: the piece for 'dry' is left out of the box word

parts.note: a cassette is a small box or case, as for jewels or tape
TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: A Friday box with no booze inside is small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken feed' usually means a trivial sum; here it is literal, a meal made of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a stew of sliced meat, classically poultry, in a white sauce: a feed of chicken.

clue.text: Ogle refined woman — wow! — mingling

indicators.note: the two pieces are mixed together, their letters interwoven

parts.note: a lady is a woman of refinement
gee is an exclamation of surprise like wow

explanation.surface: A lecher leers at a classy woman, says 'wow!' and works the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mingling' interweaves the two pieces rather than tacking one on the other; 'Ogle' is the definition, not a hint to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A glad eye is an amorous or flirtatious look, so giving one means eyeing someone suggestively.

clue.text: As cross topless shot has set back small department stores?

indicators.note: keeps inside, so the reversed piece holds the jumbled letters
with its top letter removed
put into reverse, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: used in the sense of shattered or ruined, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Cross that a topless photograph has delayed small department stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' gives STPED, 'topless' makes TPED, and SHA (from 'shot has') goes into it after the T. The letter T looks like a cross with its top arm missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a capital T has an upright and a crossbar, the form of a cross.

clue.text: 1728 is big and fat

parts.note: great means big
gross means fat or obese

explanation.surface: A number described as large and overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gross is twelve dozen, 144, and twelve of those make 1728 items, the cube of twelve.

clue.text: Generally, fruit and veg is well done!

definitions.meaning: as a rule fresh produce is healthy and nourishing for the eater

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both praises an achievement and describes food that is healthy, as produce generally is.

clue.text: Pencilled letters are inclined to be slower

parts.note: pencil leads are graded by the letters H and B, here spelled out with the word 'and'
to rake is to slope or be inclined, as a stage does

explanation.surface: Written-out letters tend to be slower to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link. 'slower' means something that slows, not 'more slow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The parking brake operated by hand slows or stops a vehicle, so it is a thing that slows.

clue.text: As at Big Sur, McCartney's axe to grind?

indicators.note: grinding breaks things down and remixes them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Beatle's instrument played hard on the Californian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Sur is a rugged stretch of the California coast. 'Axe' is musicians' slang for a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney played the four-string low-register instrument in the Beatles, his 'axe' in band slang.

clue.text: In score draw, selfsame errors the talk of the town

indicators.note: the word for 'selfsame' sits within the drawn score

parts.note: a score draw such as one-all is a tied football result with goals, here one-one
very means selfsame, as in 'the very man'
slips are mistakes

explanation.surface: In a drawn football match, identical mistakes become the gossip of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: A score draw is a British football-pools term for a drawn match where goals are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely discussed by everybody is in common conversation, which is what being the talk of the town means.

clue.text: Misguidedly names a threat for ______ as ET?

definitions.text: Misguidedly names a threat for ______ as ET?

indicators.note: wrongly guided, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these words' letters, together with the answer's, make up the fodder

explanation.surface: The alien in ET wrongly calls someone a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: NAMES A THREAT rearranges into the answer plus AS ET, so the blank is filled by the word that, with 'as ET', makes up the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of our planet is what the alien ET would call a human, and the film's humans did treat him as a threat.

clue.text: Old East European bloke raised Big John!

indicators.note: lifted, in a down clue, so the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a guy is a bloke, a man
OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for big
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: A fellow from the old Eastern bloc picked up a big man called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big John' looks like a name; it is two pieces, OS (outsize) and LAV (US slang 'john', a toilet).
explanation.definitionFit: Yugoslavia broke up in the 1990s, so a citizen of it is a former Balkan national.

clue.text: Homely glow that's apparently generated by disruptive air passenger?

indicators.note: carried inside, so the anger rides within the journey

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air
anger is the cause of disruptive behaviour, as in air rage

explanation.surface: The cosy flicker of the hearth is jokingly blamed on an unruly airline customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passenger' signals carrying inside: an angry flyer brings anger aboard the journey. Think 'air rage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The light from a hearth fire gives a cosy warmth associated with home.

clue.text: With respect, Burmese will have to go without rug

indicators.note: outside, so the two pieces surround the honorific

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, to pee
U is a Burmese honorific, a term of respect as in U Thant

explanation.surface: Politely, a man from Myanmar must go out without a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpiece worn to hide baldness is jokingly called a rug.

clue.text: See 13
Special Boards eerily able to clear beaujolais nouveau?

indicators.note: in a weird and spooky manner, so the letters come out strangely arranged
the letters of the word able are removed from the wine's name
new, so the remaining letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Spooky ouija sessions can apparently clear the new season's French red.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: BEAUJOLAIS holds the letters of ABLE plus those of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These lettered boards are used in seances to spell out supposed spirit messages, hence special.

clue.text: Perhaps releases take on what is being put about

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions
eh? is a request to repeat, like 'what?'

indicators.note: placed around, so the two letters of is surround the other piece

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Taking on something that's being spread around, perhaps like news releases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps releases' reads as re-leases, that is leases again; taking on again is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease something again is one way to engage it anew, hence 'perhaps' for an example.

clue.text: Not the ultimate in Indian grain supply?

definitions.text: Not the ultimate in Indian grain supply?

indicators.note: without, so the last letter of Indian is taken away from the fodder
used as an adverb, supply means in a supple, flexible way, so the letters are bent into a new order
the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question whether this is the best way to supply cereal in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger millet, a cereal grown widely across India, goes by this name.

clue.text: Content to run it in Greek wedding?

indicators.note: what is contained within the words, a run of letters hidden there

explanation.surface: Happy to elope to a Greek wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy'; read it as 'contents of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage joins two people together, so a wedding is a joining.

clue.text: Hobbling contest?

definitions.meaning: lame, as in a gammy leg

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lame in the leg (old-fashioned) and a match or competition.

clue.text: Pop discovered heavy, slow-moving ape up ahead

indicators.note: positioned in front, so the ape comes first

parts.note: orang is short for orang-utan, an ape

indicators.note: uncovered, so the outer letters are stripped off

parts.note: leaden means heavy and sluggish

explanation.surface: Dad found a heavy, sluggish ape walking up ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad or a bang; it is a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a sweet carbonated soft drink, and this citrus one is a classic example.
